servedVsInjected.serverRendered: ONLY the body noscript fallback. The served HTML contains exactly one GTM element, in <body> at byte offset ~540083 (the <head> ends at 312946): <noscript><iframe src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/ns.html?id=GTM-PFZPR33H" \n height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe></noscript>. Its wrapping HTML comments are NOT in the served DOM, and its whitespace differs slightly from the payload string (a space after the src quote and before `height`), i.e. it was re-serialised by Vue rather than emitted verbatim.
servedVsInjected.notServerRendered: The gtm.js loader <script> is NOT in the served <head>. Verified: the <head> substring of raw/trimming.html contains neither 'googletagmanager' nor 'GTM-'; its only 4 <script> tags are libphonenumber-js, intl-tel-input utils, intl-tel-input, and the Nuxt module entry https://stcdn.leadconnectorhq.com/_preview/zC2SjMv-.js.
servedVsInjected.injectedAtHydration:
The loader exists only as an escaped string inside the __NUXT_DATA__ payload (globalHeadTrackingCode, index 5019): "\n\n". The Nuxt app injects it client-side after hydration; the empty container
sits next to the noscript in the served body.
servedVsInjected.consequence: In the saved snapshot GTM is CONFIGURED but not yet LOADED. Any tool that reads only the server response (curl, a no-JS crawler, a static rebuild of this template) will see the noscript iframe and no gtm.js. Do not report the head script as present in the served HTML - it is not. A rebuilt control template must reproduce both halves to match behaviour: the noscript in the body, and the loader injected (or, for a static rebuild, placed in the head).
